The paper proposes a topology optimization method that considers the geometric constraint of no closed cavities for additive manufacturing.
The proposed fictitious physical model represents a fictitious steady-state heat flow with a heat source in the void domain.
The diffusion coefficient a_p should be set to a value between 1x10^2 and 1x10^3 to appropriately express the constraint satisfaction.
The small diffusion coefficient (epsilon)_p should be set to a value of ≤1x10^-5 to ensure the desired behavior of the fictitious physical field and topological derivative.
The size of the fixed design domain in the numerical examples is 1.0m x 2.0m x 1.0m.
The isotropic linear elastic material has a Young's modulus of 210 GPa and a Poisson ratio of 0.3.
In the minimum mean compliance problem examples, the diffusion coefficients are set to a_p = 1x10^1 and (epsilon)_p = 1x10^-4.
Without the geometric constraint, the optimal configuration includes a cavity that is not connected to the outside.
With the geometric constraint, the optimal configuration does not have any closed cavities and the structural type changes from a plate-like structure to a columnar structure.

The proposed method makes it possible to select an appropriate structural type in consideration of the geometric constraints, which is difficult to obtain based on a shape that was obtained without considering the geometric constraint.
The proposed fictitious field can detect and suppress closed cavities without imposing excessive constraints on the shape.

The topological derivative contains information that is close to the constraint violation state, which helps suppress oscillation between the violation state and non-violation state in the optimization process.
The proposed method can qualitatively control the minimum size of a slit for powder removal by adjusting the diffusion coefficient a_p.
The fictitious physical models are dimensionless, so the range of parameter settings will always be valid regardless of changes in the size of the design domain.
The proposed method allows for optimal design for manufacturability in the basic framework of topology optimization by introducing the fictitious physical model.
